title: Cough (acute)
summary: NICE visual summary and full guidance. Do not issue a prescription for an antimicrobial to a patient who is likely to have a self-limiting condition. Acute cough usually falls under self-limiting, i.e. when caused by a viral upper respiratory tract infection or acute bronchitis. Symptoms can last up to 4 weeks, with most people getting better within 3 to 4 weeks without antibiotics.
changeSummary: Initial transcription from Eolas Medical, Northern Ireland Primary Care Antimicrobial Guidelines (v5.119.0).
clinicalNotes: Consider a back-up prescription, or an immediate prescription in those who are identified at a face-to-face clinical examination as at a higher risk of complications (see NICE point 1.1.5).
Only offer an immediate antibiotic to those identified at a face-to-face clinical examination as systemically very unwell.
Refer to hospital or seek specialist advice if they have symptoms suggesting a more serious condition such as sepsis, a pulmonary embolism or lung cancer.
Do not offer an oral or inhaled bronchodilator/corticosteroid (unless underlying airways disease) or a mucolytic.

regimens.label: Adult 1st line (back up or immediate prescription)

components.dose: 200 mg on first day, then 100 mg once a day for 4 days
components.frequency: Once a day after first day

regimens.label: Adult 2nd line (back up or immediate prescription)
notes: Alternatives: clarithromycin tablets 250 mg–500 mg twice a day for 5 days; erythromycin tablets 250 mg–500 mg four times a day or 500 mg to 1000 mg twice a day for 5 days.
Use amoxicillin or erythromycin in women who are pregnant.

regimens.label: Child 1st line (back up or immediate prescription)

components.displayName: Amoxicillin oral suspension (or capsules in older children)
components.dose: 1 month–11 months: 125 mg three times a day; 1–4 years: 250 mg three times a day; 5–17 years: 500 mg three times a day

regimens.label: Child penicillin allergic / 2nd line (back up or immediate prescription)

components.displayName: Clarithromycin oral suspension (or tablets in older children)
components.dose: 1 month–11 years: under 8 kg 7.5 mg/kg twice daily; 8–11 kg 62.5 mg twice daily; 12–19 kg 125 mg twice daily; 20–29 kg 187.5 mg twice daily; 30–40 kg 250 mg twice daily. 12–17 years: 250–500 mg twice daily

notes: Alternatives: erythromycin oral suspension (or tablets in older children): 1 month–1 year 125 mg four times a day or 250 mg twice daily; 2–7 years 250 mg four times a day or 500 mg twice daily; 8–17 years 250–500 mg four times a day or 500–1000 mg twice daily (5 days). Doxycycline capsules 12–17 years: 200 mg on first day, then 100 mg once a day for 4 days (5 days in total).
Use amoxicillin or erythromycin in women who are pregnant.
